rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earth is usually singular because it denotes the lower realm, a quality opposed to height, rather than a count of discrete entities.
rows.anchor: أنها بمنزلة السفل والتحت ولكن وصف بها هذا المكان المحسوس فجرت مجرى امرأة زور وضيف فلا معنى لجمعهما

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The hadith about one who wrongfully takes land treats the seven earths as distinct, countable tracts, permitting the plural when parcels are specified.
rows.anchor: ومنه قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم طوقه من سبع أرضين فجمعها لما اعتمد الكلام على ذات الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens are plural because their entities, rather than the quality of height, are meant; their small number suits the sound plural, unlike earth as lower realm.
rows.anchor: وأما جمع السموات فإن المقصود بها ذاتها دون معنى الوصف فلهذا جمعت جمع سلامة لأن العدد قليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earth remains a collective singular beside the heavens because, even if multiple, it is like one small pebble compared with a desert.
rows.anchor: بل هي بالنسبة إليها كحصاة في صحراء فهي وإن تعددت كالواحد القليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earth is the abode of this world, which revelation diminishes by comparing it with the hereafter; on one view the heavens are not part of this world.
rows.anchor: كما يدخل الإنسان إصبعه في اليم فما يلعق بها هو مثال الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When heaven means the encompassing quality of above or height, it is singular, like earth, rather than a particular heaven.
rows.anchor: فإذا أريد الوصف الشامل للسموات وهو معنى العلو والفوق أفردته كالأرض بدليل قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular السماء in 10:61 reflects the comprehensive quality of height; 34:3 uses plural السماوات because context stresses God's knowledge of all His dominion.
rows.anchor: وأن له ما في السموات وما في الأرض فاقتضى السياق أن يذكر سعة علمه

words: لَا تُحَرِّكْ بِهِۦ لِسَانَكَ لِتَعْجَلَ بِهِۦٓ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command is a brief conversational interruption urging attention, like telling a listener to hear and understand, before resuming the original discourse.
rows.anchor: فهذا من باب قولك للرجل وأنت تحدثه بحديث فينتقل عنك ويقبل على شىء آخر أقبل على واسمع ما أقول وافهم عنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the unlettered Prophet moved his tongue as revelation came, he was told to reflect rather than hurry to repeat it; God would gather and preserve it.
rows.anchor: وكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أميا لا يقرأ ولا يكتب وكان إذا نزل عليه الوحى وسمع القرآن حرك لسانه

words: الْيَوْمَ يَئِسَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْ دِينِكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The announcement that the disbelievers despair of the religion is inserted within the surrounding legal discourse to encourage acceptance and practice, resistance to disbelief, and recognition of religion's completion.
rows.anchor: ووسط هذه الجملة بين الكلامين ترغيبا فى قبول هذه الأحكام والعمل بها والحث على مخالفة الكفار وموت كلمتهم وإكمال الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about necessity connects back to “that is transgression”; 6:145 makes the same sequence explicit.
rows.anchor: اتصال ﴿ فمن اضطر ﴾ بقوله ﴿ ذلكم فسق ﴾ آية الأنعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening returns from the Qur'an and its believing audience to disbelievers; contrast supplies an associative link, heightening suspense and confirming the prior discourse.
rows.anchor: فرجع إلى الحديث عن المؤمنين فلما أكمله عقب بما هو حديث عن الكفار فبينهما جامع وهمى بالتضاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection calls the contrastive link remote: believers are mentioned only incidentally, while the discourse's true subject is the Book introduced at the opening.
rows.anchor: فإن قيل هذا جامع بعيد لأن كونه حديثا عن المؤمنين بالعرض لا بالذات والمقصود بالذات الذى هو مساق الكلام إنما هو الحديث عن الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift from third-person report to direct address rebukes those who claim God has a child as though they were present before the speaker.
rows.anchor: لقد جاءوا للدلالة على أن من قال مثل قولهم ينبغي أن يكون موبخا

words: إِنَّمَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ أَوْثَانًا وَتَخْلُقُونَ إِفْكًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's rebuke uses direct second-person forms—“you worship” and “you fabricate”—as an instance of shifting from third-person narration to address.
rows.anchor: إنما تعبدون من دون الله أوثانا وتخلقون إفكا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other examples of the same shift include address to the audience in warnings, blessings, commands, and narrated scenes.
rows.anchor: وقوله ﴿ وسقاهم ربهم شرابا طهورا إن هذا كان لكم جزاء ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects classifying 5:6 as this shift: الذين is third person and has its required antecedent in آمنوا, so a second-person pronoun cannot refer back to an absent third-person group.
rows.anchor: وهو عجيب لأن الذين موصول لفظه للغيبة ولا بد له من عائد وهو الضمير في آمنوا فكيف يعود ضمير مخاطب على غائب

words: لَا يَمْلِكُونَ لَكُمْ رِزْقًا فَابْتَغُوا عِنْدَ اللَّهِ الرِّزْقَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rule that a second definite noun repeats the first applies when repetition is unintended; 29:17 deliberately repeats, as the prior repeated mention of Lord also illustrates.
rows.anchor: وهذه القاعدة فيما اذا لم يقصد التكرير وهذه الآية من قصد التكرير ويدل عليه تكرير ذكر الرب فيما قبله

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: Another explanation says إله means “the worshipped”; a derived predicate denotes its attribute, so repeating ضارب with different objects does not repeat the same predicate in substance.
rows.anchor: واجاب غيره بان اله بمعنى معبود والاسم المشتق انما يقصد به ما تضمنه من الصفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In “fighting in it is grave,” the repeated phrase comes first from the questioners and then from the Prophet's reply, so it is not repetition by one speaker.
rows.anchor: وأجيب بان احدهما حكى من كلام السائل والثاني من كلام النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وإنما الكلام في وقوعهما من متكلم واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source also lists repeated غضب, نذير, and آية as cases in which the latter occurrence refers back to the former.
rows.anchor: قالوا بلى قد جاءنا نذير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When an indefinite noun is followed by a definite one, the latter often denotes the same entity: the envoy, lamp, way, or path already introduced.
rows.anchor: إلى فرعون رسولا فعصى فرعون الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source calls 29:17 a counterexample to the rule that a following definite noun is simply identical with the prior indefinite noun.
rows.anchor: لا يملكون لكم رزقا فابتغوا عند الله الرزق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some infer that every reconciliation is recommended; the source objects that the first specific reconciliation falls under the second statement but is not its genus.
rows.anchor: فالاول داخل في الثاني وليس بجنسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source gives the shift from a particular conjecture to the general noun “conjecture” as another qualification of simple noun repetition.
rows.anchor: ما يتبع أكثرهم إلا ظنا إن الظن لا يغني من الحق شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In “grant every possessor of merit his merit,” the first فضل means the deed and the second its reward.
rows.anchor: الفضل الاول العمل والثاني الثواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source also cites “strength added to your strength” and “faith added to their faith” as further cases of repeated nouns.
rows.anchor: ليزدادوا إيمانا مع إيمانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading takes الرزق in the earlier verse to mean one's share or allotment, so no ellipsis needs to be supplied.
rows.anchor: وقيل الرزق في الآية الأولى الحظ والنصيب فلا حاجة إلى تقدير

rows.speaker: أبو الفتح
rows.claim: Abū al-Fatḥ, in al-Muḥtasib, supplies “on the deeds of the people of the Fire” as the understood complement of فما أصبرهم على النار.
rows.anchor: وقدره أبو الفتح في المحتسب على أفعال أهل النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من الموت means approaching or nearing death; although this is hard for a person, it is said when someone is driven toward what they fear.
rows.anchor: فالتقدير من مداناة الموت أو مقاربته ولا ينكر عسره على الإنسان ولكن إذا دفع إلى أمر هابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The look of one fainting from death is cited as a parallel use for the phrase about nearing death.
rows.anchor: ينظرون إليك نظر المغشي عليه من الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The trace from which the Samaritan took a handful is specified as the trace of the messenger's horse hoof.
rows.anchor: أي من أثر حافر فرس الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What God granted His Messenger from the towns means the property of the disbelievers among their inhabitants.
rows.anchor: أي من أموال كفار أهل القرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means deeds performed by people whose hearts have God-consciousness.
rows.anchor: أي من أفعال ذوي تقوى القلوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rain parable omits both a genitive noun and its complement: it compares hypocrites' condition to people caught in rain, not directly to rain itself.
rows.anchor: فإن التقدير كمثل ذوي صيب فحذف المضاف والمضاف إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition and complement are omitted: they mingled a good deed with a bad one, and another bad deed with a good one.
rows.anchor: ﴿ خلطوا عملا صالحا ﴾ 10 أي بسيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parses أكبر as elliptical for “greater than everything”; the comparison is supplied after the superlative.
rows.anchor: أي من كل شيء ﴿ فإنه يعلم السر وأخفى ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same ellipsis is illustrated by “He knows the secret and what is more hidden than the secret.”
rows.anchor: ﴿ فإنه يعلم السر وأخفى ﴾ 2 أي من السر

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī allows أكبر to be cut off from its complement deliberately, expressing absolute rather than comparative superiority; on this reading there is no ellipsis.
rows.anchor: وكلام الزمخشري في المفصل يقتضي أنه مما قطع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فكيف in the witness-gathering verse confirms what precedes and underscores what follows: if God does not wrong people in this life, how will their state be in the hereafter?
rows.anchor: فإنه توكيد لما تقدم وتحقيق لما بعده على تأويل إن الله لا يظلم الناس شيئا في الدنيا فكيف في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same فكيف heightens awe by asking what their state will be when every community has a witness; the Prophet also used كيف to evoke a future condition for ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿAmr.
rows.anchor: وقول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لعبد الله بن عمرو كيف بك إذا بقيت في حثالة من الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كيف can function as a verbal noun in questions about how God extends shade or revives the earth after its death.
rows.anchor: كيف يحيي الأرض بعد موتها

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh treats كيف in كيف تكفرون as adverbial, “in what state”; al-Akhfash instead parses it as a circumstantial expression, “in what state are you disbelieving?”
rows.anchor: وعلى الحال عند الأخفش أي على حال تكفرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After فكيف إذا جئنا, one may supply a noun such as your state or conduct, or a verb such as “what will you do?”
rows.anchor: فإن شئت قدرت بعدها اسما وجعلتها خبرا أي كيف صنعكم أو حالكم وإن شئت قدرت بعدها فعلا تقديره كيف تصنعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some treat كيف as semantically conditional, with its response omitted and inferred from context; this is linkage rather than formal conditional inflection, though Kufans say it governs the jussive.
rows.anchor: وجوابه في ذلك محذوف لدلالة ما قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A verb may be omitted after كيف; in كيف وإن يظهروا عليكم the implied wording is كيف توالونهم.
rows.anchor: وقد يحذف الفعل بعدها قال تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām has governing and non-governing forms; the non-governing lām has ten functions, including definiteness, distance, emphasis, and other discourse roles.
rows.anchor: وتجيء لعشرة معان معرفة ودالة على البعد ومخففة وموجبة

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: For the definite article, Sibawayh treats lām alone as the marker; al-Khalīl analyzes it as two letters, with a hamzat qaṭʿ linked through frequent use. Definiteness may be anaphoric or generic; some add a relational function.
rows.anchor: فالمعرفة التي معها ألف الوصل عند من يجعل المعرفة اللام وحدها وينسب لسيبويه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The written alif marks a word considered through concrete, lower, or knowable reality; its omission marks a metaphysical, attributive, or higher aspect beyond sense.
rows.anchor: فإن الألف تحذف فى الخط علامة لذلك واعتبار من جهة ملكية حقيقية فى العلم أو أمور سفلية فإن الألف تثبت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an details verses established in the comprehensive Book, so it is nearer to understanding and clearer in revelation; its alif is written, while كتاب omits it.
rows.anchor: فالقرآن أدنى إلينا فى الفهم من الكتاب وأظهر فى التنزيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In two verses the word قرآن is written without alif because it is synonymous with the Book mentioned immediately before; their “so that you may reason” also signals its conceptual aspect.
rows.anchor: هو فيهما مرادف للكتاب فى الاعتبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that it is in the Mother of the Book, exalted and wise, further associates the revelation with the comprehensive Book.
rows.anchor: في أم الكتاب لدينا لعلي حكيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The general orthography كتاب omits alif, with four exceptions where the word has a more particular referent or relation to revelation.
rows.anchor: وكذلك كل ما فى القرآن من الكتاب وكتاب فبغير ألف إلا فى أربعة مواضع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In “for every term there is a Book,” كتاب denotes the specific record of appointed terms, narrower than the absolute Book or one attributed to God.
rows.anchor: فإن هذا كتاب الآجال فهو أخص من الكتاب المطلق أو المضاف إلى الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Book assigned to a town before its destruction is the specific record of the destruction of towns, narrower than the record of appointed terms.
rows.anchor: فإن هذا كتاب إهلاك القرى وهو أخص من كتاب الآجال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Book in “recite what was revealed to you” is more particular than a general book; the author says the particular is more manifest in revelation.
rows.anchor: فإن هذا أخص من الكتاب الذى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In 27:1 Book follows Qur'an, whereas in 15:1 Qur'an follows Book; the former refers to the particular revelation as a detailed presentation of the universal Book.
rows.anchor: هذا الكتاب جاء تابعا للقرآن والقرآن جاء تابعا للكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur'anic verses divide into those clear by themselves and those requiring explanation; many examples of the first kind are listed.
rows.anchor: ما هو بين بيفسه بلفظ لا يحتاج إلى بيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verses needing clarification are explained elsewhere in the Qur'an or by the Prophet's Sunnah, which was appointed to explain revelation to people.
rows.anchor: أو فى السنة لأنها موضوعة للبيان قال تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an leaves many practical details to explanation, including zakat amounts and conditions, prayer counts and times, and the rites and prohibitions of pilgrimage.
rows.anchor: والثانى ككثير من أحكام الطهارة والصلاة والزكاة والصيام

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report in both Ṣaḥīḥ collections says the Prophet, answering Ibn Masʿūd's companions, explained zulm in 6:82 as shirk and cited Luqman's words in 31:13.
rows.anchor: قالوا يا رسول الله وأينا لا يظلم نفسه قال ليس ذلك إنما هو الشرك ألم تسمعوا ما قال لقمان لابنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In حتى إذا جاؤوها وفتحت أبوابها, حتى requires completion; the implied wording repeats جاؤوها before the doors are opened.
rows.anchor: لا بد لها من تمام وتأويله حتى إذا جاءوها جاءوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's oath by the Prophet's life discloses his greatness and standing with God; al-Qushayri says an oath is by something either virtuous or beneficial.
rows.anchor: ليعرف الناس عظمته عند الله ومكانته لديه قال الأستاذ أبو القاسم القشيري

rows.speaker: أبو القاسم القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayri classifies the Mount and the secure city as objects of oath for their virtue, and the fig and olive as beneficial.
rows.anchor: الأستاذ أبو القاسم القشيري في كنز اليواقيت والقسم بالشيء لايخرج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine oaths may name God, His acts, or created things; they may be explicit, marked by an oath lām, or implicit in meaning.
rows.anchor: أحداها بذاته كقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God swears by groups of angels at the openings of al-Saffat, al-Mursalat, and al-Naziat.
rows.anchor: بطوائف الملائكة في أول سورة الصافات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some parse the bāʾ in “do not associate with God” as an oath, supplying an omitted لا تشرك before بالله; most omitted-verb oaths use wāw instead.
rows.anchor: وقال الباء باء القسم وليست متعلقة تشرك وكأنه يقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although some take بما عهد as an oath, the author prefers reading it as a request, not an oath.
rows.anchor: والاولى أن يقال إنه سؤال لا قسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A proposed pause at لي makes بحق begin a separate oath: “By God, if I said it.”
rows.anchor: ما يكون لي أن أقول ما ليس لي بحق إن كنت قلته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Omitting the final nūn of the verb marks a small or humble starting point from which creation develops toward what only God can encompass; the human begins as a despised drop.
rows.anchor: حذفت النون تنبيها على مهانة مبتدأ الإنسان وصغر قدره بحسب ما يدرك هو من نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The incompleteness of worldly existence compared with the afterlife is illustrated by calling the latter the true life.
rows.anchor: إن الدار الآخرة لهي الحيوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In وإن تك حسنة, the dropped nūn marks even a good deed of tiny measure as small in itself, though God orders and multiplies it.
rows.anchor: حذفت النون تنبيها على أنها وإن كانت صغيرة المقدار حقيرة فى الاعتبار فإن إليه ترتيبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shortened إن تك in Luqman's example likewise marks how minute the seed-sized matter is.
rows.anchor: إن تك مثقال حبة من خردل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the question to the condemned, the dropped nūn marks the messengers' gradual ascent from sense evidence to reason and remembrance, and from ignorance to certainty.
rows.anchor: جاءتهم الرسل من أقرب شىء فى البيان الذى أقل من مبدأ فيه وهو الحس إلى العقل إلى الذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nūn remains in ألم تكن آياتي تتلى عليكم because the act of reciting the signs has reached completion.
rows.anchor: فإن كون تلاوة الآيات قد أكمل كونه وتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nūn remains in the question about God's spacious earth because the condition has fully come to be.
rows.anchor: هذا قد تم كونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nūn remains in لم يكن الذين كفروا because their state of not separating continued to its specified endpoint, the coming of clear proof.
rows.anchor: هذا قد تم كونهم غير منفكين إلى تلك الغاية المجعولة لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here the nūn is dropped because even the beginning or least amount of benefit from their faith is denied, and thus all benefit is denied.
rows.anchor: انتفى عن إيمانهم مبدأ الانتفاع وأقله فانتفى أصله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because Arabs were challenged to produce a sura, then ten suras, repeating stories across many suras preempts a claim that one story need only be matched once.
rows.anchor: لما سخر العرب بالقرآن قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeated tellings of Moses and Pharaoh differ in wording, order, and detail because each version carries a nuance found only there; unlike earlier scripture's separate single tellings, Joseph's story is collected in one sura.
rows.anchor: فقد يوجد في ألفاظها زيادة ونقصان وتقديم وتأخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeated stories with varied wording do not become awkward or tiresome, unlike human speech.
rows.anchor: فيها مع سائر الألفاظ لم يوقع في اللفظ هجنة ولا أحدث مللا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Addition, omission, and rearrangement keep repeated accounts from having identical wording and sounding merely repeated.
rows.anchor: ومنها أنه ألبسها زيادة ونقصانا وتقديما وتأخيرا ليخرج بذلك الكلام أن تكون ألفاظه واحدة بأعيانها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Distributing a story's meanings across changing repetitions draws eloquent listeners through their love of novelty, giving each version a fresh share of pleasure.
rows.anchor: ومنها أن المعاني التي اشتملت عليها القصة الواحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The varied compositions expressing related story meanings amazed the Prophet's contemporaries and point to God's inexhaustible speech, beyond any finite number of words.
rows.anchor: فعرفهم الله سبحانه أن الأمر بما يتعجبون منه مردود إلى قدرة من لا يلحقه نهاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's non-exhaustion holds even under the impossible supposition of every earthly tree as pens and seven seas as ink; the passage tests how لو relates a condition to its consequence.
rows.anchor: فعدم النفاد في الآية الكريمة واقع على تقدير كون ما في الأرض من شجرة أقلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited conditionals imply that if angels came or the dead spoke, the disbelievers still would not believe; if they heard, they would turn away, which is even likelier.
rows.anchor: فإن التولي عند عدم الإسماع أولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The praise of Suhayb—if he did not fear God, he would not disobey—presupposes his non-disobedience; denying that would contradict the praise's context.
rows.anchor: نعم العبد صهيب لو لم يخف الله لم يعصه فنفي العصيان ثابت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account takes such لو clauses as linking the condition and result without implying that the result is otherwise impossible: non-exhaustion and Suhayb's obedience hold even more under the opposite condition.
rows.anchor: دعوى أنها في مثل هذه المواضع أعنى الثابت فيها الثاني دائما إنما جاءت لمجرد الدلالة على ارتباط الثاني بالأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author concludes لو makes its condition impossible and links it to the result, but does not establish whether that result is independently true; commonly neither condition nor result occurs.
rows.anchor: والتحقيق أنها تفيد امتناع الشرط كما سبق من الآيات الشريفة وتحصل أنها تدل على أمرين

rows.speaker: الإمام فخر الدين
rows.claim: Fakhr al-Din rejects impossibility as part of لو's meaning and treats it as linkage alone, citing the conditional about God knowing good in them and their turning away if made to hear.
rows.anchor: وجعلها لمجرد الربط واحتج بقوله تعالى
